category_override: answered elsewhere; confirmed or written up here
notes: Yes: Pereira (ELA 16, 2007) proved every potentially nilpotent full sign pattern is spectrally arbitrary; N1 and N2 follow from potential nilpotence for full patterns (trace and trace of the square). Re-derived: regular nilpotents are dense among real nilpotents, the characteristic-polynomial map is a submersion there, scaling covers all polynomials. Outside Lean: the whole argument (implicit function theorem, real Jordan form).

sources.cite: R. Pereira, Nilpotent matrices and spectrally arbitrary sign patterns, Electron. J. Linear Algebra 16 (2007) 232-236
sources.what: every potentially nilpotent full sign pattern is spectrally arbitrary

sources.cite: I.-J. Kim, D. D. Olesky, B. L. Shader, P. van den Driessche, H. van der Holst, K. N. Vander Meulen, Generating potentially nilpotent full sign patterns, Electron. J. Linear Algebra 18 (2009) 162-175
sources.what: restates Pereira's theorem; order-3 full pattern with N1, N2 that is not spectrally arbitrary
